entries.title: A positive inverse escape moment does not give a finite crossing mean
entries.statement: DRAFT audit material, independent review pending. In dimension one let right-jump probabilities be iid, equal to 3/4 with probability 3/4 and to 1/4 otherwise. With rho_i=(1-p_i)/p_i and q=P_{0,omega}(T_{-1}=infinity), harmonic scale gives q^-1=1+sum_{k>=0} product_{j=0}^k rho_j. For lambda>=0, E q^-lambda is finite exactly when lambda<1: for 0<lambda<1, it is at most 1/[1-(3/4)3^-lambda-(1/4)3^lambda]; at lambda=1 Tonelli and E rho=1 make it infinite. In particular E q^-1/2<=4+2sqrt(3), although the first crossing mean is infinite and the walk's speed is zero. This same q appears in the layer-iid d>=2 lift omega(x,+e1)=p_x1/2, omega(x,-e1)=(1-p_x1)/2, omega(x,+/-ej)=1/[4(d-1)] for j>=2; the lift is not site iid. A small positive inverse moment alone therefore cannot replace an integrable duration estimate. This is not a C0041 counterexample and does not refute the public claimed proof's stronger crossing estimate.
assumptions: Critical one-dimensional iid law, outside C0041
In the lifted version: iid layers, not iid sites
Independent and different-model review not complete

relations.rationale: The critical law isolates why a small positive reciprocal-survival moment is weaker than the duration premise needed for positive speed; its d>=2 lift explicitly lacks site iid.
